info.title: fmd-web API
info.description: fmd-web server API (DESIGN.md §10). Contract-based: every schema here is generated from the zod source of truth (server/src/api/schemas.ts); the committed snapshot (server/src/api/openapi.snapshot.json) fails CI on unintended drift. Errors use one typed envelope: { error: { code, message, details? } }.

get.summary: Module registry with capability + known-broken flags
get.description: One row per registered module (§9 module_state registry columns): identity, §5.1 options (combobox options carry `items`; the STORED value is the item INDEX), and §5.10 capability detection incl. the D3 known-broken flag ids. `live_scrape_fallback` (§6.8) marks modules declaring both directory events — browsable without an FMD2-DB catalog via the live walk. `catalogInstalled` joins the CatalogStore receipts (§6.4 getMeta): the site-first Browse picker renders it as a per-site chip and drives auto-provisioning from it (additive).

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

put.summary: Enable/disable a module, set options, cookies and the proxy override
put.description: Option values are validated against the module descriptors: checkbox → boolean, edit → string, spinedit → integer, combobox → integer item INDEX within `items` range (§5.1). Unknown option names are rejected with 400. `proxy` sets the per-module proxy override (null clears it back to "inherit the global proxy"; §9/§10 settings, SetProxy field semantics).

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

post.summary: Bulk enable/disable many modules at once
post.description: FMD2 Websites-tree bulk parity (pas:6400 Select All/Unselect All + per-category checkboxes): one enable/disable write over many module_state rows through the SAME update seam (option/cookie/proxy state untouched). Targets: `ids` (explicit list), OR `category` (exact category match), OR neither (every registered module — the global select-all/none). Unknown ids/categories resolve to an empty target set (`updated: 0`, never a 404 — a sweep is idempotent).

200.description: The resolved module set after the write + count

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

post.summary: Manually probe one site's reachability (per-row Check)
post.description: [site-availability] ONE probe of the module RootURL through the module's own engine HTTP path (worker-isolated in production, module-appropriate headers). Classification matches the opportunistic traffic seam exactly: transport-class failures (DNS, connect refused, timeout, TLS) and the HTTP 5xx/523 family write `unreachable` + a short reason; 2xx/3xx answers write `reachable` (a later success flips an unreachable record back — self-healing, no timers); HTTP 4xx (403/429 anti-bot, rate-limit) writes NOTHING — verdict `none`, the record stays unchanged (origin alive but possibly blocking). Deliberately single-site: batch check-all is a documented deferral (anti-bot risk + low value; revisit when cold-start friction is felt) and nothing is ever scheduled or re-probed in the background.

200.description: Probe verdict + the resulting (possibly unchanged) availability record

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

get.description: One row per module account: username, enabled flag and the module AccountState (§5.2 account-status constants). The password is write-only — it is sealed at rest (FMD_WEB_SECRET, AES-256-GCM) and never returned.

put.summary: Create/replace the account for one module
put.description: Module-scoped account upsert (FMD2 keeps exactly one account per module). Omitted `password`/`cookies` KEEP the stored values — the credential never round-trips through the API. All three fields are sealed with FMD_WEB_SECRET before the write.

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

delete.summary: Remove the account for one module
delete.description: Deletes the sealed account row (§9 `account`). The module_state cookies are NOT touched.

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

post.summary: Run the module OnLogin flow (event runtime)
post.description: Dispatches the §5.2 `Login` event with the account-status constants bound and MODULE.Account seeded from the sealed row; the handler-set `MODULE.Account.Status` and `MODULE.Account.Cookies` are read back and persisted (account row + §5.3 module_state cookies). Engine/dispatch failures are 502 upstream_error.

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

409.description: Account disabled or the module binds no OnLogin handler

502.description: The module OnLogin run failed (typed error envelope)

get.summary: Global proxy config + output defaults + browser sidecar profile state
get.description: The §9/§10 settings projection: the global proxy (SetProxy five-string semantics, httpsendthread.pas:838-874 — type HTTP|SOCKS4|SOCKS5, the empty type is "no proxy"), the output defaults (FMD2 Save-to parity subset: default archive format zip/cbz/pdf/epub + chapter filename template, honored on NEW download jobs) and the §5.11 browser profile state (enabled ⇒ the D2 sidecar is wired and the satisfied §5.10 known-broken flags are dropped from /api/modules).

put.description: Full replacement with SetProxy semantics: a config with a non-empty type requires a host; the all-empty config is the SetNoProxy path. Per-module overrides (PUT /api/modules/{id} proxy) take precedence for their module.

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

put.summary: Replace the output defaults (format + chapter rename template)
put.description: FMD2 Save-to options parity (additive, the server-supported subset): `format` picks the §7.3 packer for NEW download jobs (zip/cbz/pdf/epub — FMD2's None loose-images mode is deferred; the §7.1 library model is one packed artifact); its default is cbz — the Komga/Kavita scan-target convention (DESIGN-NORTHSTAR §2 EXIT/§3). `chapterNameTemplate` is the FMD2 custom rename (edOptionMangaCustomRename) with the %NUMBERING%/%CHAPTER%/%WEBSITE%/%MANGA%/%AUTHOR%/%ARTIST%/%FILENAME% placeholder vocabulary — a pure settings change, no code edit; '' keeps the chapter-name fallback. The default template is the FROZEN `<numbering> <chapter>` decision (DESIGN-NORTHSTAR §7): `%NUMBERING% %CHAPTER%` — the zero-padded 1-based list ordinal plus the site's chapter label; the defaults are frozen after the scan-target story (later changes need a migration event). %NUMBERING% is NEVER a number parsed from the chapter title (the §5 killed-ideas ruling; the no-chapter-number-parsing gate enforces it). PDF quality and the unicode rename option details are deferred (D16 streaming packer is DCT passthrough — see docs/UX-PARITY.md).

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

put.summary: Replace the Performance group (FMD2 Connections subset, additive)
put.description: [parity-sweep] M10: requestTimeoutSeconds seeds the HTTP pipeline default (module code may still override per request); retryCount is the per-image retry budget; threadsPerChapter is the per-chapter image-worker width (FMD2 MaxThreadPerTaskLimit); parallelChapters is the download-lane slot count and applies at SERVER START (lane slots are fixed at boot). Persisted in app.db (app_settings).

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

put.summary: Replace job-history retention (auto-delete after N days, additive)
put.description: [parity-sweep] M2: auto-delete finished job history after N days; 0 = keep forever. Drives the periodic prune sweep (hourly; a change applies on the next sweep). Persisted in app.db (app_settings).

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

put.summary: Replace the filename policy (D5 mode, additive)
put.description: [parity-sweep] M4: true = Linux-normalized filenames; false = the FMD2-desktop parity default. Precedence: the FMD_NORMALIZE_PATHS env / --normalize-paths flag OVERRIDES the setting (env > setting > parity). Persisted in app.db (app_settings).

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

put.summary: Replace diagnostics settings (log enable + level, additive)
put.description: [parity-sweep] M13: structured-log enable + minimum level, applied live to the running logger. The live log VIEWER is v0.4; /metrics + the runbook are linked from the Diagnostics section. Persisted in app.db (app_settings).

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

put.summary: Replace the favorites scheduler settings (interval + startup check)
put.description: FMD2 Options → Updates parity (additive): `intervalMinutes` is the OptionAutoCheckFavIntervalMinutes analog — 0 disables scheduled checks, other values apply LIVE to the running scheduler (idle favorites re-arm under the new cadence). `checkAtStartup` is OptionCheckFavoritesAtStart — it gates the next boot's initial sweep. Persisted in app.db (app_settings) so it survives restarts.

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

put.summary: Replace the outbound webhook config (url + secret + event toggles)
put.description: THE outbound webhook (DESIGN-NORTHSTAR §3 Pipeline: "at most one webhook, zero channel adapters") — one generic JSON POST destination; translating events into any chat/push service is the receiving operator's business, never adapter code in this app. `url` is the OFF state when empty (default); a non-empty url must be http(s) (typed 400 otherwise). A non-empty `secret` HMAC-SHA256-signs every delivery: X-FMD-Signature: sha256=<hex> over the exact request body. `events` toggles the three runtime classes independently: chapter.downloaded (individual, per finalized chapter), favorites.digest (ONE summary per completed check sweep) and failure.digest (per-SITE coalesced check failures — a dead site with 50 favorites produces ONE entry per 15-minute digest window, never 50). Delivery is fire-and-forget with 2 retries then drop (logged) — advisory and lossy-tolerated; the inbox remains the source of truth. Persisted in app.db (app_settings `webhook.config`).

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

post.summary: Deliver a webhook.test sample event through the real signer + transport
post.description: The test-send action: ONE awaited full delivery cycle (initial attempt + up to 2 retries) of a `webhook.test` sample envelope — the only place webhook delivery is awaited (real events stay fire-and-forget). Returns the honest report: `delivered`, the POST `attempts` count, and the last HTTP `status` / `error` when not delivered. 409 when no url is configured. Mounted only when the notifier seam is bound (the runtime always binds it).

409.description: No webhook url configured — set one via PUT /api/settings/webhook first

post.description: Runs the §2/§6 module syncer: fetch at the pinned commit, validate via the Init pass, atomically swap the tree, record sync_state, and return the deterministic sweep summary.

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

get.summary: Catalog rows ordered by jdn DESC (§6.6)
get.description: Page-number browse over the read-only attached catalog. No popularity ordering exists (D14). §6.8 fallback: with no catalog installed, modules declaring both directory events are served LIVE from their §5.8-normalized directory walk (TTL-cached, update-lane isolated) — every response carries `source: "catalog" | "live"` so the UI can badge it.

200.description: Page of catalog entries (source discriminator per §6.8)

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

503.description: Live scrape update lane is shutting down

get.description: Page-number browse over the read-only attached catalog. §6.8 fallback: catalog-less modules serve their §5.8-normalized directory walk live (title-ordered NOCASE); `source` discriminates.

200.description: Page of catalog entries (source discriminator per §6.8)

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

get.summary: FTS5 search with cursor pagination (§6.5, §10) + FMD2 filter panel (additive)
get.description: Sanitized FTS MATCH over the sidecar, ranked; `cursor` continues a previous page (opaque, query-bound — it carries the FULL filter state). Catalogs are read-only after install, so cursors stay stable. FMD2 Filter-panel parity (frmMain.pas:3400, additive): `q` is optional when any filter is set (filter-only pages skip the MATCH and order by jdn DESC); `authors` is a LIKE-contains over the authors column; `genres` (repeated params or one comma-separated value) joins per `genresMode` — `all` (FMD2 rbAll default) ANDs the LIKE clauses, `any` (rbAny) ORs them; `genresExclude` (same wire forms, the `!` custom-genre prefix) composes one AND-NOT-LIKE per excluded genre (audit (b)2 fix — excludes AND among themselves regardless of genresMode; a genre in both lists resolves to exclude-only); `newDays` is the only-new window (jdn > JDN(today) - newDays, FMD2 cbOnlyNew). Prefix-LIKE (`x%`) is a documented non-goal: FMD2 semantics are contains (`%x%`). §6.8 fallback: catalog-less modules search their §6.8-normalized directory-walk snapshot in memory (title/alttitles/summary terms, exact status, substring genre) with the SAME cursor scheme; `source` discriminates the channel.

200.description: Ranked page of catalog entries (source discriminator per §6.8)

400.description: Malformed cursor

503.description: Live scrape update lane is shutting down

get.summary: Scoped union search over installed catalogs (FMD2 cbSearchFromAllSites parity + D1 §2 scope)
get.description: FMD2 parity (frmMain.pas:3411-3416): the union runs simultaneously over every INSTALLED catalog of every enabled site — a LOCAL catalog union, never live scraping. Per-site FTS windows (width 2×limit) are merged by a documented deterministic total order — (normalized title, site id, link) — so result order and cursor bytes are identical under any permutation of the site set. `cursor` continues each site window (base64 of per-site consumed-row counts, bound to the issued filter state INCLUDING the scope; page-size independent). Every row carries `site` + `siteName` (FMD2 shows the source Website on union rows, frmMain.pas:5170). Partial failure is TYPED, never silent: a broken catalog yields the rest of the union plus a `warnings[]` entry naming it; enabled sites without an installed catalog are excluded and surfaced in `excluded[]` (reason `no-catalog`) so the UI chip can explain why. `facets[]` carries per-site totals for the count chips. [fuzzy-javelin-pearls] SCOPE (D1 §2 ENTER): `scope=all` (the default — every enabled site with an installed catalog, answered from the local index with ZERO network) or `scope=preferred` (the persisted user-ordered allowlist filters the participation set; the allowlist order orders `facets[]`). An explicit `sites` list (the specific multi-select, comma-separated or repeated param) WINS over the named scope — the tightest scope; unknown registry ids are a typed 400 naming them, known-but-disabled sites drop out (invisible, union parity). The response echoes the effective `scope`. Repeated identical pages are served from a SHORT-TTL cache (30 s, bounded, generation-bumped by preferred-sites writes).

200.description: Merged page of site-tagged entries + facets/warnings/excluded + scope echo

400.description: Malformed cursor

get.summary: The preferred-sites allowlist in canonical order (D1 §2 ENTER)
get.description: ONE global, user-ordered list of site ids the operator actually uses (single user per instance, R2/D1 §4.1 — no per-user dimension exists). The ORDER is canonical (D1 §3): it fixes scope ordering, presentation order in the site picker, and duplicate-title resolution order. Site names are not carried — /api/modules is the name authority and consumers join it (rows read `preferred: true` for members). Never a gate: a dead preferred site dims wherever it renders (availability hint) and stays fully visible.

404.description: Route (preferred-sites service not mounted) not found

put.summary: Replace the preferred-sites allowlist (the one-decision add, D1 §2)
put.description: Full-list REPLACEMENT — the submitted ordered list IS the next canonical order (a UI add/remove is one decision sent as the next full list). Unknown registry ids are a typed 400 naming them; duplicates keep their FIRST position (canonical). Bumps the /api/search cache generation so scoped pages never serve against a stale allowlist. GET never mutates; this PUT is the one write surface.

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

404.description: Route (preferred-sites service not mounted) not found

post.summary: Normalized live manga info + the downloaded-chapter set (§5.8, cached)
post.description: Runs the module GetInfo event and applies the §5.8 post-processing pipeline (last-occurrence-wins dedup); responses are cached per (moduleId, url) for the configured TTL. `downloaded` (MangaPage parity — FMD2 downloaded-chapters tint/hide) carries the chapter LINKS already recorded in the `downloaded_chapters` ledger for this manga: it is computed at response time — never cached with the info snapshot — so a just-finished download flips the set on the next call, cache hit or not. [parity-sweep] M14 (FMD2 edURL parity): `moduleId` is OPTIONAL — a url-only body resolves the module by RootURL host match (registry lookup). Unknown host → 400 `no_site_match` ("no site matches this URL"); multiple sites on one host → 400 `ambiguous_site` naming the candidates. The response embeds the serving `moduleId` so the client can navigate to the manga page.

200.description: Normalized MANGAINFO state + downloaded chapter links

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

get.description: Streams one cover image for the ADDRESSED module: the url a module GetInfo returned (e.g. `http://fmcdn.mfcdn.net/store/manga/…/cover.jpg?token=…&ttl=…`) is validated against that module's permitted hosts (RootURL host + its registrable domain + a curated known image-CDN allowance — foreign or malformed urls are 400, this is never an open proxy), then fetched with the module HTTP posture (engine User-Agent, AcceptImage, Referer = module RootURL for hotlink-checked CDNs; http:// urls try https first with a deliberate http fallback for https-less origins) and the upstream image/* bytes are served with the upstream content-type. cache-control max-age derives from the url token ttl (1h floor, 24h cap); an on-disk cache under FMD_WEB_DATA_DIR/covers is keyed by the TOKEN-FREE normalized url so re-issued tokens hit cache (total size capped, oldest entries pruned). Non-image content or failed origin hops are typed 502s; an unknown module is the typed 404 envelope. Plain GET — never credential-gated (the *arr ordering; covers are not secrets).

200.description: The cover image bytes (upstream image/* content-type)

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

502.description: Cover origin failed or returned a non-image

post.summary: Create a download job (idempotent, §10)
post.description: With `idempotencyKey`: an identical-key replay returns the ORIGINAL job with 200 while it is live (queued/running/retry); key reuse with a DIFFERENT payload returns 409. Re-enqueueing a TERMINAL original (done/failed/cancelled) starts a FRESH job chained under the same key (`<key>#<n>`, 201) — the re-download semantic; the fresh attempt resumes from the persisted chapter markers ('D' slots skip their images). Fresh creates return 201. MangaPage parity options (additive): `paused` (FMD2 cbAddAsStopped, frmMain.lfm:1110) creates the job queued-but-held — the download lane will not claim it until POST /api/jobs/{id}/resume; `saveTo` (FMD2 edSaveTo, frmMain.pas:5613) is a custom save directory that REPLACES the `library/<manga>` prefix at finalize (relative paths resolve against the library root).

200.description: Idempotent replay of the original job

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

409.description: Idempotency key reused with a different payload

post.summary: Batch download-all create (idempotent per manga, §10)
post.description: The browse row-menu Download-all (FMD2 pmMangaList miMangaListDownloadAll, frmMain.lfm:5798) as ONE request per manga instead of one chatty request per chapter. `chapters: "all"` resolves the live chapter list through the SAME cached §5.8 info path POST /api/info uses; an explicit link array enqueues exactly that selection in the given order (no info fetch). `idempotencyKey` is REQUIRED: every per-chapter create derives `<key>:<index>` (index in the resolved chapter order), so the whole batch replays as one unit — identical replay while any original is live returns the SAME jobs with 200 + `replayed: true` (the double-submit case); a shifted/different chapter sequence under the same key surfaces the per-chapter 409 different-payload conflict; TERMINAL originals chain fresh attempts (`<key>:<index>#<n>`) exactly like the single create — the re-download semantic. `paused`/`saveTo` apply to every chapter job.

200.description: Full replay — every chapter returned an existing live job

201.description: Created batch (at least one fresh/chained job)

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

409.description: Batch key reused with a different chapter sequence

get.summary: Job list with filters + keyset cursor (Downloads parity)
get.description: Newest-first page (`limit` ≤ 100). `cursor` is the keyset boundary (the last job id of the previous page) — stable under concurrent inserts: newly created jobs never shift pages. Downloads parity filters (FMD2 tsDownload filter tree + search box, web-adapted): `states` (csv multi-select of the §7.1 states), `q` (case-insensitive substring over the job's mangaTitle/chapterName) and `addedFrom`/`addedTo` (inclusive created-at calendar days, UTC — the client maps FMD2's History windows Today/7d/Month/Older and custom From/To into this range). `state` (single) predates the multi-select and stays for back-compat. R5 arrival adds `since` (ISO 8601 UTC timestamp): a floor on the row's LAST TRANSITION (`updatedAt`) — combined with `state=done` it selects chapters FINISHED since the timestamp, the 'While you were away' summary's download-news source.

400.description: Malformed cursor

get.description: The current §7.1 row (state, progress, error) — the polling fallback beside the WS stream.

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

delete.summary: Delete a download job row (FMD2 delete task | delete task + data)
delete.description: Removes the job row in ANY state (a running chapter aborts first). `?data=true` (miDownloadDeleteTaskData parity) ALSO removes the finalized artifact the job recorded at done — the library file and its `library_files` row; the default (miDownloadDeleteTask) keeps the download on disk. The response echoes the removed snapshot plus `dataDeleted`.

200.description: The removed job snapshot + artifact outcome

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

post.summary: User-cancel a download job (§7.1)
post.description: queued/running/retry → cancelled (200). A running chapter aborts its in-flight images and persists the 'W'/'D' markers, so the next enqueue of the same chapter resumes (only the remaining images are fetched). A terminal row is 409 — nothing to cancel.

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

post.summary: Lift the add-as-stopped hold on a download job (cbAddAsStopped parity)
post.description: A job created with `paused: true` sits in `queued` with the hold set — the download lane does not claim it. This endpoint clears the hold (200, `paused` absent thereafter); the lane picks the row up like any other queued job. Terminal rows are 409; resuming a job without the hold is an idempotent no-op returning the current snapshot.

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

post.summary: Apply one downloads-tab task action (FMD2 pmDownload parity, web-adapted)
post.description: ONE typed-union route over the per-job task actions (FMD2 pmDownload menu, frmMain.lfm:5538-5617). `pause` — resume-able stop (miDownloadStop): a queued row gains the hold (`paused: true`, not claimable), a running/retry row user-cancels with markers persisted. `resume` — the inverse (miDownloadResume): a held queued row lifts the hold; a cancelled row re-enqueues a FRESH chained attempt that resumes from the persisted markers. `retry` — failed → fresh chained attempt. `redownload` — done → fresh chained attempt (miDownloadRedownload). `disable` — hold a scheduled-but-not-running row (queued only). `enable` — lift that hold (queued+held only). Holding a held row / lifting an unheld one is an idempotent no-op. Every ILLEGAL application is 409 with the typed envelope carrying `{job: {id, state, paused}, action}` details.

200.description: The resulting job snapshot (fresh row for re-enqueue semantics)

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

409.description: Action illegal in the job current state (state matrix)

post.summary: Toolbar bulk op: Resume all / Pause all / Delete completed (FMD2 tsDownload toolbar)
post.description: `{action: "pause"|"resume", scope: "all"}` — Stop All / Resume All (frmMain.lfm:291-339): pause holds every queued row and cancels every running/retry row; resume lifts every hold and re-enqueues every cancelled row (markers resume). `{action: "delete", scope: "completed"}` — Delete completed (miDownloadDeleteCompleted = RemoveAllFinishedTasks): removes every `done` row, artifacts KEPT (per-row delete+data is the explicit choice). Idempotent: a settled queue returns `affected: 0`. Other scope/action pairings are 400.

400.description: Scope does not apply to this action

get.description: Newest-first page over the library rows (one per packed chapter file, `library/<manga>/<file>` — the flat series layout; duplicates live under `<manga> [<module>]`). `cursor` is the keyset boundary like /api/jobs. [file-state] Rows carry additive stat-verified fields (`state` downloaded|missing, `verifiedAt`, root-relative `path` + `absolutePath`, `mtime`) and the Library page chips ride `filter`: `all` (default), `missing` (stat-verified missing rows, keyset-paginated) or `orphans` (serves the LAST RESCAN's persisted orphan list — orphan truth is rescan truth, never a live walk per listing).

400.description: Malformed cursor

get.summary: Per-title chapter file listing (Files section — metadata only)
get.description: [file-state] The server-storage window for one title: every tracked chapter file keyed off the ONE downloaded-chapters ledger (ledger links without rows surface as missing — e.g. an FMD2 import mapped the ledger without files on this machine), each carrying its recorded path (root-relative display form; the absolute path rides alongside for copy-path), size, mtime, and the verified_at stamp. Verification is LAZY: entries stale >15 min are re-stat-verified on open; `?refresh=1` forces re-verification. Orphans (files under the title's convention directory no ledger row claims) close the listing. METADATA ONLY — no endpoint on this surface serves file bytes; every path is realpath-clamped to the downloads root and dotfiles are skipped.

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

post.summary: Rescan library — reconcile the ledger against disk (persisted diff report)
post.description: Walks the configured downloads root via the shared directory-walker seam (dotfiles skipped, symlink escapes clamped out) and reconciles the `library_files` ledger against what is actually on disk. CONSERVATIVE re-linking for moved-within-root files only: an exact-filename match at a different directory, or the app's own output naming convention (`<manga>/<file>` — the effective folder, module-suffixed for duplicates) hitting exactly one candidate. Ambiguous matches (two+ same-name candidates) are NEVER auto-linked — they surface as an orphan+missing pair for the operator to resolve (v1: delete the ledger entry or ignore the orphan; interactive adoption is deferred). The diff report (re-linked with former paths, missing with former paths + candidates, orphans with path/size/mtime, counts) is persisted and re-served by GET /api/library/rescan. Optional `moduleId`+`url` scope the reconcile to one title (the per-title variant on the manga detail Files section).

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

get.summary: The last persisted rescan diff report
get.description: Re-serves the report the last POST /api/library/rescan persisted (the Library page's orphan filter and report surface read here). `report` is null until the first rescan runs.

Streams the artifact bytes (application/octet-stream, attachment Content-Disposition). The ZIP/CBZ structure is client-validatable (central directory walk). [file-state guardrail] the recorded path is realpath-clamped to the downloads root — a path resolving outside it (tampered row, relocated symlink) is a typed 403 `path_outside_library_root`, dotfiles are never served; missing files stay the 404.

400.description: Request failed schema validation (typed error envelope)

Favorites upsert idempotently keyed by module id + RootURL-canonicalized mangaUrl through the ONE favorites import path (offline seed: statuses, current chapter, downloaded lists, ledger rows merge — re-importing the same file creates no duplicates). Unmapped site ids are listed and skipped, never fatal. The report enumerates created/updated/unchanged/skipped with reasons and every setting not imported.

get.description: The ONE deployment-wide token (Sonarr/Radarr model — never lists, never per-user); the app's ONLY credential since the optional-password mode was removed. Returns the stored value (`null` when the FMD_WEB_API_TOKEN env pin owns the secret — read it from the deployment environment instead) and the envManaged flag (UI shows 'Managed via environment', hides Regenerate). The app is open (*arr auth-None semantics): this read is anonymous — front the app with a reverse proxy (Authelia/Authentik/PocketID) when it must not be.

post.summary: Rotate the single API token in place (audit-logged)
post.description: Generates a new 32-byte-hex value and replaces the old one IMMEDIATELY — the old key is rejected on the next request, so update your scripts right after rotating (docs/API.md key-rotation runbook). Audit-logged as a settings change (the log never carries the value). 409 when FMD_WEB_API_TOKEN pins the token (rotate the env instead). Reachable unauthenticated (*arr semantics: the token is a script key on an open deployment — runbook §API token).

200.description: The new token state (value included, shown once)

409.description: Env-pinned (FMD_WEB_API_TOKEN) — rotate the secret in the deployment environment

The §4/§15 series in Prometheus text format (version 0.0.4): queue depth per lane, job throughput/failure by state, per-module request latency + error counts, corpus pass rates, engine pool RSS + GC stats, sync progress, and the expression-failure WARN dedup counters. Mounted only when a metrics registry is bound (the production assembly always binds one).

bearerToken.description: R4 SINGLE app-wide API token (Sonarr/Radarr model): `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. One value per deployment — auto-generated on first start (an *arr-style script key), rotated in Settings → API (regenerate) or pinned via FMD_WEB_API_TOKEN (env > settings). The app's ONLY credential (the optional-password mode was removed): every route serves unauthenticated (*arr auth-None semantics — put Authelia/Authentik/PocketID via reverse proxy in front for user auth) and the token is ACCEPTED wherever presented. Constant-time verified; never multiple/per-user tokens.
